title: Before You Escalate a Supply Risk
primary_reader: A supply-chain practitioner who has received a changed supplier date and needs to separate an unreliable signal from a customer-facing exception before calling the wrong meeting.

reader_contract.reader_moment: A supplier date moved, a customer need-by may be exposed, and the team is about to optimise cost before agreeing on what is actually at risk.
reader_contract.reader_payoff: A four-gate pre-meeting check that turns a vague supply-risk escalation into one visible sequence of questions.
reader_contract.decision_question: What must be true before this date risk becomes a joint customer exception?
reader_contract.glance_3s: Before you escalate a supply risk: four customer-first gates.
reader_contract.scan_10s: Validate the date, test customer exposure, check recovery, then decide the exception jointly.
reader_contract.use_30s: Identify the first unanswered gate and bring that fact—not a guessed recovery date—into the next meeting.

scope.in_scope: A proposed working method for preparing a supply-date exception conversation.
scope.not_for: It is not a predictive delivery model, a universal release rule, a freight-approval policy, or evidence that a recovery option will work.
scope.assumptions: The reader adapts the checks to their own date-quality rules, customer commitments, decision rights, and available recovery options.

truth_contract.basis: Tiger direction TS-20260807-01 for this internal lab (customer need-by across credible scenarios; block false precision; joint KAM and Purchasing Manager exception ownership) plus a clearly labelled internal four-gate method synthesis. See claim-ledger.json; the exact flow is not asserted as a deployed or universal workflow.
truth_contract.scope: The guide structures a conversation and surfaces unresolved facts; it does not claim an observed deployment or outcome.
truth_contract.not_claiming: It does not guarantee an on-time outcome, calculate freight economics, or prove that the four checks are complete in every operating system.

method_contract.inputs: Supplier confirmation quality, customer need-by, feasible recovery options, and accountable owners.
method_contract.validation: Validate date reliability and test whether any credible scenario misses need-by before treating a recovery path as a promise.
method_contract.human_decision_boundary: If recovery cannot close a credible customer gap, KAM and Purchasing Manager jointly decide the exception and next owner.

visual_argument.spatial_claim: A changed supplier date becomes a customer exception only after a reader works through four ordered checks.
visual_argument.why_shape_truthful: A one-way four-gate flow is appropriate because each later question depends on the preceding check: unreliable date, customer exposure, recovery, then joint exception.
visual_argument.anti_misread: Do not read the flow as a predictive algorithm, a fixed duration, a freight-approval sequence, or a guarantee that the final owner can resolve the issue.

modules.title: Date reliability
modules.reader_action: Verify whether the supplier date is credible before converting it into a customer-facing promise.

modules.title: Customer exposure
modules.reader_action: Test whether any credible date misses customer need-by before discussing cost optimisation.

modules.title: Recovery check
modules.reader_action: Make available stock, alternate supply, split delivery, and approved freight visible without promising that any option works.

modules.title: Joint exception
modules.reader_action: Escalate the remaining customer exception to KAM and Purchasing Manager when recovery cannot close a credible gap.

claims.text: A changed supplier date should be validated before it becomes a customer promise.

evidence.rationale: A proposed operating-method guardrail. Claim-ledger.json links the source context and marks the exact four-gate wording as a bounded synthesis, not an empirically proven universal rule.

claims.text: Customer need-by is a separate check from supplier-date reliability.

evidence.rationale: A conceptual distinction inside the stated working method. Claim-ledger.json links its customer-first source context; no outcome or numerical claim is made.

claims.text: Recovery options should be examined without converting them into an unverified recovery promise.

evidence.rationale: A bounded planning and escalation practice. Claim-ledger.json marks the exact wording as a proposed synthesis, not a claim that any recovery option succeeds.

claims.text: A remaining credible customer gap routes to a joint KAM and Purchasing Manager exception decision in this proposed working method.

evidence.rationale: Tiger-approved project-specific operating direction, linked in claim-ledger.json and visibly framed as a proposed method rather than a claimed industry standard.

boundary_or_exception.statement: A date without a reliability check is a guess. This is a meeting check—not a predictive model.
boundary_or_exception.reader_response: When any credible scenario misses need-by and recovery cannot close the gap, bring the unresolved fact to a joint exception decision rather than inventing certainty.

next_action: Before the next meeting, ask: What must be true for this customer date to hold?

motion.reason: Motion earns its place only as a companion: a single risk signal can travel through the four gates in the exact order that the reader must test them.
motion.communicates: A changed supplier date is not yet a customer exception; it becomes one only after reliability, exposure, and recovery checks are visible.
